calls.reason: Epoch measured China's capability lag in months, and CNBC reported similar assessments from Hassabis and Huang near publication. Together these support a modest model lead, despite the much larger US investment advantage.
Google and Alibaba disclosures show continued participation in 2026. That coexistence cannot settle Marcus's open-ended prediction that neither country could exclude the other.

Ars Technica documents GPT-4's uninterrupted Arena leadership from May 2023 to March 2024, well beyond a few months. The faster leadership changes reported in 2025 do not sustain the categorical claim.
Pew and Alibaba support adoption and overlapping products, while DeepSeek and Epoch document capability gaps. The packet does not establish whether those gaps materially undermine practical parity.

DeepSeek's December report acknowledges disadvantages in knowledge, token efficiency and complex tasks; Epoch independently finds persistent US capability leadership. Together these weigh against the assertion that nobody has a real technical advantage.
